issues.description: File filter '*.exe' hides conda executables on macOS/Linux
issues.detail: In confpage.py the browsefile is created with filters='*.exe'. On macOS/Linux the conda/mamba/micromamba executables have no extension, so the file dialog will hide them by default and force users to switch filter manually. Filter should be platform-aware (e.g. '*.exe' on Windows, '*' or no filter elsewhere).

issues.description: validate_conda uses substring match that accepts unrelated executables
issues.detail: The check `any(tool in out.decode().lower() for tool in ['micromamba','mamba','conda'])` matches any binary whose --version output contains 'conda' anywhere (e.g. 'anaconda-client', 'conda-build', random text). It also assumes communicate() returns bytes; if run_program returns text mode this raises. Match should be stricter (startswith or regex) and decode defensively.

issues.description: os.access(X_OK) check breaks on Windows for .exe files
issues.detail: os.access(path, os.X_OK) is unreliable on Windows and may return False for legitimate .exe files depending on ACLs. Since this is the primary platform for the '*.exe' filter, validation may reject perfectly valid conda.exe paths and prevent users from configuring the feature.

issues.description: Empty conda_path still treated as valid when custom_conda enabled
issues.detail: In kernelspec.py the code reads `conda_path` if `custom_conda` is True, but conda_path defaults to ''. An empty string is falsy and falls through to the not-found error, which is okay, but the user gets the 'set the path in Preferences' message even though they already enabled the custom-conda checkbox with no path — confusing UX. Consider validating at save time or showing a clearer message.

issues.description: No validation that custom conda_path actually exists at kernel-launch time
issues.detail: kernelspec.py trusts the stored conda_path without re-checking that the file still exists or is executable. If the user deletes/moves the binary after configuring, the failure mode is a downstream subprocess error rather than a clear SpyderKernelError. A quick os.path.isfile check with a targeted message would improve diagnostics.

issues.description: Hardcoded stylesheet margin bypasses theme system
issues.detail: `conda_path.setStyleSheet('margin-left: 3px')` injects a raw stylesheet rule into a single widget, bypassing Spyder's qt-stylesheet/theme infrastructure used elsewhere in the codebase. This can collide with active themes and complicates future restyling. Prefer layout-level margins or the existing styling helpers.

review.summary: The PR cleanly threads a new custom-conda preference through config, UI, and kernelspec, but several details will bite real users. The file dialog filter is hardcoded to '*.exe', which is wrong on macOS/Linux where conda binaries have no extension. The validator's substring match accepts any executable whose --version mentions 'conda' and depends on bytes from run_program, and os.access(X_OK) is unreliable on Windows where the filter actually applies. Smaller concerns: stale conda_path at kernel launch, confusing empty-path UX, and a hardcoded stylesheet that bypasses theming.
